notes: **2026-09-05** — (worktree `rf-imp-E`, branch `feat/legacy-orphan-users-and-ocr-review`, off `origin/master` `17e81c2c` = #626; code commit `e848f19a`) — **THE BACKFILL TOOL LEARNS A SECOND, MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE TASK (`--deactivate-orphan-users`), AND THE OCR GATE GETS ITS OWNER RULING.** Two independent follow-ons from the close-out, no schema change and no migration. **(1) Orphan users.** Everything the tool did until now repairs a NULL `tenantId` by DERIVING one from a parent row; a NULL-tenant `User` has no such parent, so it can never be backfilled at all. The prod census (2026-09-05) found six: three `SUPER_ADMIN`s, which are platform accounts and correct as they are, and three April-2026 `TENANT_ADMIN` leftovers that would 401 at login. **Owner decision 2026-09-05: those are DEACTIVATED, never deleted** — the row, its foreign keys and its audit trail all survive and the change is reversible by hand. The new task reads and writes ONLY `WHERE "tenantId" IS NULL AND "role" <> 'SUPER_ADMIN'`, writes only `User.status`, and never a `tenantId`. The inactive value is **`INACTIVE`**, read from `enum UserStatus { ACTIVE INACTIVE SUSPENDED }` in `apps/api/prisma/schema/tenancy.prisma` and mirrored by `UserStatus` in `packages/types/index.ts` (there is no `UserStatus` union in `packages/types/api/enums.ts` — that file does not carry it). Report line is `User <id> role=<role> status=<status> created=<t> updated=<t> -> <verdict>`: id, role, enum status and timestamps only, and the listing does not even SELECT `email`/`username`/`password`/`googleId`, so output discipline is enforced by the query rather than by remembering not to print things. Pure classifier `classifyOrphanUser({role, status, deletedAt}) → {verdict, status, reason}` over `ok` | `refuse: already inactive` | `refuse: super admin` | `refuse: deleted`, strongest-refusal-first so a row that trips two rules is reported by the one that matters (`refuse: super admin` is defensive — the listing's own WHERE already excludes the role, and it is refused AGAIN here so a future edit to the query cannot deactivate a platform account silently). `orphanUserUpdateSql()` is `UPDATE "User" SET "status" = $1, "updatedAt" = now() WHERE "id" = $2 AND "tenantId" IS NULL AND "role" <> 'SUPER_ADMIN' AND "status" = $3 RETURNING "id"` with `$1 = INACTIVE`, `$3 = ACTIVE` — every clause re-states a precondition the report displayed, which is exactly what makes a re-run a no-op and a row changed under us a rollback; `"updatedAt"` is set explicitly because Prisma's `@updatedAt` is client-side and does not fire on raw SQL. `--live` takes the same `--backup-attested` plus a typed `DEACTIVATE <n> USERS` (the jest-gated `BACKFILL_CONFIRM_TOKEN` applies unchanged). **The two tasks now share ONE write path**, the new `confirmAndApply(updates, phrase, applied, rollbackReason)` — confirmation, TTY check, `SET default_transaction_read_only = off`, `BEGIN`, per-row `RETURNING` check, rollback + **exit 4**, `COMMIT`, the `=== APPLIED ===` block — so neither task can grow a looser confirmation or an unchecked update by being edited alone; the tenant path's rollback wording ("was no longer NULL-tenant") is preserved verbatim through `rollbackReason`, and `--dry-run` printing is now `printStatements`, driven by `params.length` so the user task's third bound value prints without a second copy of the loop. **`--backfill-tenants` exists for exactly one reason:** the tenant backfill is the DEFAULT, so naming it explicitly is the only way to ASK for both — and asking for both is **exit 2** before any connection is opened, never a silent choice of one. `--json` gains a `task` field on both paths. Header comment, `--help` and `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` (one sentence, in the NULL-tenant follow-on's own paragraph) all carry the ruling. **(2) The OCR add-on gate**, `apps/api/src/billing/addon-gate-registry.ts`: the `ocr` row's `reviewBy` moves `2026-10-15` → **`2027-03-31`** and its `backfill` note is replaced with the owner's sentence verbatim — `Owner decision 2026-09-05: OCR available to all tenants; gate stays dark until OCR is monetized; no grants required`. The field names on `AddonGateEntry` really are `reviewBy` and `backfill`; `state` stays `dark`, so P1c (dark `reviewBy` not expired) and P1d (`ocr` is dark) both still pass and **`addon-gate-registry.spec.ts` needed no edit at all** — it never pinned the date or the note literally, only the `YYYY-MM-DD` shape and the expiry rule. Coverage: the unit spec goes 38 → **52 tests** (B6a–B6f every verdict branch plus the precedence, B7a–B7d `buildOrphanUserUpdates` + the exact statement + no `DELETE` and no `tenantId` write, B5i/B5j spawn-level exit 2 for the mutual exclusion and for `--live` without an attestation, B5k the help text, B5l source pins on the WHERE and on the SELECT list), and the DB lane gains **D8** — a NULL-tenant `TENANT_ADMIN`, a NULL-tenant `SUPER_ADMIN` and a tenanted `OPERATOR` are seeded under the run's `e2e-backfill-` prefix; only the first is listed at all (the other two never appear, because the WHERE hides them rather than refusing them), no `@example.invalid` address reaches stdout, `--dry-run` shows the one guarded statement with `$1 = INACTIVE / $3 = ACTIVE`, `--live` with `DEACTIVATE 1 USERS` sets it `INACTIVE` while leaving its `deletedAt`/`tenantId` and the other two rows untouched, and the re-run is "nothing to do"; teardown deletes `User` by prefix before the `Tenant`.
